intent: The panel itself, portalled over the page, pinned to the edge its Drawer names and dismissible by a swipe toward that edge.
typical_uses: A form, a filter set or a record's details in a panel rising from the bottom edge
A full-height panel at the left or right edge that the user swipes away

dont_use_when.situation: An edge panel with no swipe gesture
A popup centered over the page
A floating panel anchored beside its trigger rather than to the viewport edge

invariants.text: The panel and its backdrop are in the DOM only while the drawer is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed drawer renders nothing.

Without `container`, the panel portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the panel only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.
The panel takes its edge and its swipe handle from the enclosing Drawer's `side` and `showSwipeHandle`, stamping the edge as `data-side`; rendered outside a Drawer it throws.

The panel takes its accessible name from the DrawerTitle inside it and its description from the DrawerDescription, through `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`; without a title, pass `aria-label` on DrawerContent.
Unless `initialFocus` says otherwise, opening moves focus to the panel itself rather than to the first control inside it.

The panel draws its DrawerBackdrop only while the root's `modal` is exactly `true`, and no prop switches it off separately; where that backdrop is not drawn for a nested drawer (see DrawerBackdrop), the primitive's transparent backdrop still blocks the page under it.

`top` and `bottom` panels span the full width with a height sized to the content, or to the full cap when the root has `snapPoints`, capped at the viewport height minus 6rem; `left` and `right` panels span the full height at 75% of the width, capped at 24rem from a 640px viewport up. Only the edge that faces the page gets a border, and no corner is rounded.

Children render in an inner content region, not in the forwarded panel element, so `className` styles the panel and not that region; the region has a var(--space-6) padding, spaces its children var(--space-6) apart in a column and hides overflow on both axes, so content taller than the panel is cut off rather than scrolled.

The panel slides in from its edge and back out, following the pointer during a swipe; under `prefers-reduced-motion` drawer.module.css drops the transform, height and filter transitions, so the panel appears and disappears without motion while the backdrop keeps its fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Build a modal drawer with no DrawerClose inside the panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place a DrawerClose in the panel, such as in DrawerFooter; the panel has no built-in close button, and a modal drawer needs a close control inside it so touch screen reader users can leave it

anti_patterns.dont: Leave out DrawerTitle for a cleaner look
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render a DrawerTitle and hide it visually through its `className` when the design shows no heading, so the panel keeps an accessible name

anti_patterns.dont: Put a body taller than the panel straight into DrawerContent
anti_patterns.do_instead: Wrap the long body in a scroll container of its own, such as a ScrollArea, since the panel's content region clips instead of scrolling

a11y.by: the primitive's Drawer.Popup renders the role from Base UI's dialog store, `dialog`; drawer.test.tsx asserts getByRole('dialog') once the trigger is clicked and that Escape on it removes it ("closes on Escape")

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the panel portals into; an explicit null renders no panel until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

initialFocus.states: initialFocus picks the element focused on open - left out, the panel itself; true for the first tabbable element, or the panel when it holds none; false for no move; a ref to an element; or a function of the opening interaction type
initialFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus picks the element focused on close - true for the trigger or the previously focused element, false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the closing interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the panel's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the panel's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, transitionStatus, expanded, nested, nestedDrawerOpen, nestedDrawerSwiping, swipeDirection, swiping). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through drawer.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside DrawerContent as the full-viewport layer that tracks the swipe; it blocks pointer events only while the root's `modal` is `true`.
Composed inside DrawerContent as the padded content region that holds the children, styled by drawer.module.css.

good.title: A bottom panel with a title, a body and footer actions
A panel portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: The edge set on the panel, as for a sheet
bad.why: DrawerContent takes no `side`; the edge is the root's prop, so this panel still opens from the bottom.
